title: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

sections.label: Female rate improvement
sections.summary: The rate improved from 58.1% to 62.6% over 10 years but still lags behind males.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years, it has improved from 58.1% to 62.6%, but it still lags behind the rates for males.

sections.label: Unadjusted gender pay gap
sections.summary: The Ministry's 2018 statistics put the unadjusted gender pay gap at 16.3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry's 2018 statistics, the unadjusted gender pay gap is 16.3%.

sections.label: Singapore adjusted gender pay gap
sections.summary: Singapore's adjusted gender pay gap is 6% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Singapore's adjusted gender pay gap is 6% in 2018.

sections.label: Iceland Equal Pay Standard
sections.summary: In 2018 Iceland passed the Equal Pay Standard requiring companies with 25 or more employees to prove equal pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In 2018, Iceland passed the Equal Pay Standard legislation, which requires companies with 25 or more employees to prove that they pay employees of all genders equally for the same work or work of equal value.

sections.label: Iceland pay gap closure
sections.summary: Iceland's pay gap closed by 3.4% after the legislation was passed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Iceland's pay gap closed by 3.4% subsequent to this passing of the legislation.

sections.label: Paid family care leave employers
sections.summary: Employers offering paid family care leave doubled from 15% in 2012 to 30% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The number of employers offering paid family care leave in Singapore has doubled from 15% in 2012 to 30% in 2020.

sections.label: Paid statutory caregiving leave
sections.summary: The speaker hopes to see paid statutory caregiving leave implemented for all workers in the longer term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In the longer term, I hope to see the implementation of paid statutory caregiving leave for all workers.

sections.label: Older workers re-employment acceptance
sections.summary: Between 2017 and 2021, around 97% of resident employees were offered and accepted re-employment contracts after retirement age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: And I am heartened that our older workers do appreciate our efforts in doing so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I understand from the Ministry that between 2017 and 2021, around 97% of resident employees were offered and accepted re-employment contracts after reaching the retirement age.

sections.label: Older workers fewer training opportunities
sections.summary: Six out of 10 workers felt older workers were given fewer training opportunities than younger ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Yet six out of 10, or of all workers, were of the view that older workers were given fewer training opportunities as compared to the younger ones.

sections.label: Reinstating WorkPro scheme
sections.summary: The speaker suggests reinstating WorkPro, which gave companies grants of up to $425,000 for age-friendly workplaces retaining older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Perhaps, there is now a renewed need to reinstate WorkPro, which was previously implemented as a scheme for companies to receive grants of up to $425,000 to implement age-friendly workplaces with an emphasis on retaining older workers.

sections.label: CareersFinder beta version launch
sections.summary: CareersFinder beta, launched in last year's third quarter, uses skills and jobs data and AI to help workers find upskilling and career opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The CareersFinder beta version was launched in the third quarter of last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It uses the data on skills adjacencies and jobs churn in the workforce to help workers discover the personalised upskilling needed and identify possible career opportunities based on their individual profiles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: By harnessing the power of artificial intelligence (AI) and the data, it is hoped that the efficacy of job matching can be improved and friction reduced.

sections.label: Support for involuntarily unemployed jobseekers
sections.summary: The speaker notes that details of the upcoming support measure for involuntarily unemployed jobseekers are still to be finalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: On the upcoming support to assist the involuntarily unemployed jobseekers, I know the details of the support measure is still to be finalised.

sections.label: Temporary support for involuntarily unemployed
sections.summary: Temporary financial support for the involuntarily unemployed is not new in Singapore, and ComCare provides it for some residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Temporary financial support for the involuntarily unemployed is not something new in Singapore and for some residents, the ComCare does just that.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Credit Scheme expansion
sections.summary: The speaker commends expanding the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme, which aids businesses in supporting higher wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, firstly, I commend the expansion of the Government's Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS), which significantly aids businesses in supporting higher wages.

sections.label: Local Qualifying Salary rise
sections.summary: The Local Qualifying Salary rose from $1,400 to $1,600 in Budget 2024, and the speaker asks how it will support more lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The rise in Local Qualifying Salary (LQS), as announced in Budget 2024, from $1,400 to $1,600 indicates broader cross-sector backing to uplift lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, as the PWM expands across additional sectors and wage ladders commence from an average of $2,650 for an entry-grade security officer and $1,915 in the food and beverage (F&B) sector, how will LQS support a greater number of lower-wage workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I seek MOM to share the number of lower-wage workers expected to experience wage increases due to the elevated LQS.

sections.label: Temporary foreign workforce quota increases
sections.summary: The speaker proposes temporary quota increases tied to commitments in human capital development, local worker training, and the IHRP human capital diagnostic tool programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As part of the strategy to ensure that foreign workforce policies foster business growth while enhancing collaboration with local talent, I propose implementing temporary quota increases contingent upon commitments to human capital development and local worker training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Furthermore, I suggest that the temporary quota be linked to a commitment to participate in the Institute of Human Resources Professionals' (IHRP's) human capital diagnostic tool (HCDT) professional programme and to implement its recommendations.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits not legislated
sections.summary: Retrenchments more than doubled in 2023 to 14,320 cases, yet retrenchment benefits are not enshrined in legislation for any worker category.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, according to the preliminary estimates released by MOM, retrenchments in Singapore have more than doubled in 2023 from 2022 to 14,320 cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With the threat of retrenchment for our workers all too real, it comes as a surprise to many Singaporeans that the right to retrenchment benefits is not enshrined in legislation here in Singapore for any category of worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the LifeSG guide on retrenchment benefits, the prevailing norms on paying retrenchment benefits are around two weeks to one month for each year of service, with unionised companies seeing one month of salary for each year of service.

sections.label: Mandating retrenchment benefits review
sections.summary: The Minister confirmed 2017 survey figures on retrenchment benefits, and the speaker asks MOM to review mandating retrenchment benefits for hand and heart workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister confirmed that according to the MOM's survey on retrenchment benefits in 2017, around 90% of establishments which retrenched workers paid retrenchment benefits while more than 70% of them paid benefits which met or exceeded prevailing norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of the respectable number of employers according to the Retrenchment Benefits 2017 report who are already providing retrenchment benefits meeting or exceeding the prevailing norms, I ask MOM to review its position on retrenchment benefits and progressively consider mandating retrenchment benefits for hand and heart workers to nudge employers to do so.

sections.label: Master tradesmen earnings and NTUC model
sections.summary: Master-level tradesmen can earn upwards of $8,000 a month, and NTUC has started a career progression model for such trades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: From our discussions with our trade associations and guilds, master-level tradesmen can earn upwards of $8,000 a month, particularly if they become business owners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: To this end, NTUC has started work on the career progression model to better the viability of such trades as livelihoods.

sections.label: Review of CCP training allowance rates
sections.summary: With the SkillsFuture training allowance of up to $3,000 per month, MOM is suggested to review current CCP training allowance rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Third, with the SkillsFuture training allowance support just announced, which will be up to $3,000 per month for Singaporeans to undergo programmes at our IHLs, I suggest for MOM to review the current CCP training allowance rates during the training stint and period.

sections.label: Updates on Fair Consideration Framework and COMPASS
sections.summary: MOM is asked for updates on the Fair Consideration Framework, triple weak watchlist, TGFEP cases, COMPASS, and EP qualifying salaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On the same note, can MOM also update us on the Fair Consideration Framework, the status of the triple weak watchlist, and the number and type of cases reported, investigated and closed at the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practice (TGFEP)?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I also wish to ask if the Minister has any updates, now that COMPASS has been in action for the past six months, and the review of the Employment Pass (EP) qualifying salaries?

sections.label: Fresh graduate median salary increase
sections.summary: The Graduate Employment Survey shows median gross monthly salary for fresh graduates in full-time permanent employment rose 2.7% to S$4,313 from S$4,200.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Based on the latest Graduate Employment Survey, the median gross monthly salary among fresh graduates in full-time permanent employment increased by 2.7%, to S$4,313 from S$4,200 in 2022.

sections.label: SOL bonus points in COMPASS
sections.summary: SOL in COMPASS offers 10 to 20 extra points toward the 40 required for an EP, and its effectiveness is questioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Chairman, SOL in the COMPASS EP framework offers a pathway to acquire 10 to 20 extra points towards the 40 points required for an EP, beyond the standard metrics, to ease the filling of known skill gaps in our economy with foreign labour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: To gauge its effectiveness so far, I would like to ask: (a) what percentage of EP applications, since September 2023, have taken advantage of the bonus points prospective EP applicants receive; (b) has publishing SOL increased the absolute quantity or quality of applications to these occupations compared to pre-COMPASS?

sections.label: Earning gains after training programmes
sections.summary: Evaluations found earning gains of 14% to 38% about a year after training, persisting five to 11 years after participation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The evaluations revealed substantial earning gains of 14% to 38% for participants about a year after training completion, with gains persisting from five to 11 years after participation in the programme.

sections.label: Foreign workforce policy update
sections.summary: The Minister is asked for an update on foreign workforce policies supporting business needs and fair local competition, and on managing Work Permit holder inflow given constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide an update on how our foreign workforce policies will continue to support our business needs while ensuring that local workers can continue to compete fairly for good jobs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: And while the number of Work Permit holders have rebounded post COVID-19, how does the Government intend to manage the inflow of Work Permit holders, given the resource and infrastructure constraints?

sections.label: WFL direct discrimination coverage
sections.summary: The Tripartite Committee recommended WFL cover only direct discrimination, which the speaker says is inconsistent with CEDAW and CRPD obligations to prohibit all discrimination forms.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, the Tripartite Committee recommended that WFL only cover direct discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The laws of many countries already prohibit all these forms of discrimination, and the Tripartite Committee's recommendations are inconsistent with our obligations under international law, including Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) and Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), which require us to prohibit all forms of discrimination.

sections.label: Gender pay gap legislation
sections.summary: The speaker is disappointed WFL lacks a gender pay gap mechanism and reiterates the WP call for employers with 10 or more employees to report pay gaps.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Next, on the gender pay gap, I was disappointed that WFL does not include any mechanism to address this.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Other developed economies have taken steps to legislate salary and transparency to address the gender pay gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I reiterate the WP's manifesto's call, that employers with 10 or more employees should be required to report to MOM the gender pay gap for the same job description.

sections.label: Job advertisement wording prohibition
sections.summary: MOM accepted the Committee's recommendation to prohibit words or phrases in job advertisements indicating a preference for a protected characteristic.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On information to be provided by jobseekers, MOM has accepted the Committee's recommendation to prohibit the use of words or phrases in job advertisements that indicate a preference for a protected characteristic.

sections.label: Seniors covered by MRSS
sections.summary: The Progress Singapore Party welcomed the Budget announcement that these seniors will now be covered by the MRSS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Progress Singapore Party (PSP) welcomed the announcement in this year's Budget that these seniors will now be covered by the MRSS.

sections.label: CPF investment returns transparency
sections.summary: The PSP urges the Government to be transparent about returns earned on investing CPF savings and to give this back to CPF members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The PSP shares their views and urges the Government to be transparent about the returns it has earned on investing our CPF savings and find a way to give this back to CPF members.

sections.label: Two options for Government
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government can consider setting up two options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can the Government consider setting up two options?

sections.label: Call for Government decision
sections.summary: The passage states the Government has had almost eight years to study this and calls for a decision soon.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But the Government has had almost eight years to study this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to make a decision soon.

sections.label: Channel interest savings to low balances
sections.summary: The passage asks whether interest savings can be channelled to higher interest for low balances by raising the threshold.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If this is not about saving money, can the Government channel any interest savings towards paying higher interest for those with low balances, for example, by raising the threshold for additional 1% interest from the first $60,000 to the first $100,000, or pegged to the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS)?

sections.label: CPF Investment Scheme and LRIS
sections.summary: The passage states financial instruments exist under the CPF Investment Scheme and calls for the long-delayed LRIS to be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There are already certain financial instruments available for members to invest their CPF balances under the CPF Investment Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, for the benefit of all Singaporeans' retirement, we need to ensure that the long-delayed LRIS is implemented.

sections.label: Reform OA interest formula
sections.summary: The passage repeats a call to reform the OA interest formula, last changed in 1999 from 50-50 to 80-20.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like to once again repeat my call for us to reform the long-outdated and archaic formula in which OA interest is computed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This was last changed in 1999, when the ratio of fixed deposits to savings was updated from 50-50 to 80-20, to reflect the longer duration that CPF OA monies remained with CPF Board.

sections.label: Review CPF interest rates
sections.summary: The passage states CPF deems deposit interest rates 0.66% for August to October 2023 and hopes the Government reviews CPF interest rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, despite much higher market rates for both fixed deposits and savings deposits, the CPF deems the level of deposit interest rates to be an unbelievable 0.66% for the period from August 2023 to October 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The least we can do is to reflect prevailing rates in the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will proactively review CPF interest rates to ensure their relevance in the prevailing operating environment.

sections.label: CPF Special Account interest
sections.summary: CPF contributions earn up to 4.08% per annum on the Special Account, giving Singaporeans a secure retirement avenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: With CPF contributions earning up to 4.08% per annum on the SA, Singaporeans benefit from a secure avenue for retirement adequacy.

sections.label: CPF closure and ERS impact
sections.summary: The passage asks how many CPF members will be affected by the closure and how many would benefit from raising the ERS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: How many CPF members will be affected by this closure?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: And how many CPF members would benefit from the raising of the ERS?

sections.label: Top-up yearly limit
sections.summary: The current limit is up to $600 top-up per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: The current limit is up to $600 top-up per year.

sections.label: HPS applications not approved
sections.summary: In the past three years, about 1.2% of HPS applications were not approved due to serious pre-existing medical conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the past three years, about 1.2% of HPS applications were not approved due to serious pre-existing medical conditions.

sections.label: Paid childcare leave eligibility
sections.summary: Under the Child Development and Co-Savings Act, working parents are eligible for up to six days of paid childcare leave a year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Currently, under the Child Development and Co-Savings Act, working parents are eligible for up to six days of paid childcare leave a year.

sections.label: Parental care leave entitlement
sections.summary: Civil Servants have two days of parental care leave, but the private sector has no equivalent entitlement and voluntary employer offers are just 13%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While Civil Servants have two days of parental care leave, a benefit that half of the Service exercises and an average of taking both days, there is no equivalent entitlement for the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Some employers have been willing to voluntarily offer such leave, but the share is trifling, at just 13%.

sections.label: Paid leave for only child
sections.summary: Proposes including two days of paid leave for the only child of aged parents and singles living with elderly parents.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As a start, we can include two days of paid leave for the only child of aged parents as well as singles living with their elderly parents.

sections.label: Perimenopause effects at work
sections.summary: A NUH study extrapolated to the mid-life working population suggests up to 388,800 women may bear perimenopause ill-effects at work, so employers should accommodate them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Based on a National University Hospital (NUH) study and extrapolating for the current mid-life working population, as many as 388,800 women may be bearing the ill-effects of perimenopause at work It is important for employers to recognise and accommodate these changes and foster a supportive work environment that addresses the unique needs of these women.

sections.label: Caregiving leave for women workers
sections.summary: Asks whether more caregiving leave and expanded leave coverage can support women workers, given caregiving duties and 260,000 women of economic age not in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Given that women traditionally take on the brunt of caregiving duties at home and that there are some 260,000 women of economic age not in the workforce, more must be done to support women workers to stay or return to the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider the provision of more caregiving leave to support our workers in an ageing Singapore and can the coverage of existing leave policies be expanded to include a wider range of family members requiring care?

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Will there also be additional support for women returners in the form of more paid training support to ensure a smooth transition back to the workforce?

sections.label: Guarding against FWA rejections
sections.summary: Asks what measures the Ministry will take to guard against employers rejecting flexible work arrangement requests without fair and proper consideration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: In an introduction of the upcoming Tripartite Guidelines for FWA requests, what measures will the Ministry take to guard against employers rejecting without fair and proper consideration on employees, rejecting requests for FWAs citing business reasons?

sections.label: FWA guidelines for older workers
sections.summary: Asks whether the upcoming Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests will include considerations for older workers needing reduced and flexible hours.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Will the upcoming Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests include considerations for older workers who require both reduced and flexible work hours due to age-related health issues?

sections.label: Updates on FWA guidelines
sections.summary: Asks for updates on flexible work arrangement guidelines and how adoption can be encouraged and potential harnessed for senior workers, mobility-challenged residents, caregivers and women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Does the Minister have any updates on the guidelines on FWAs and how its adoption in the public and private sector can be encouraged?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: How do we harness the potential of senior workers, mobility-challenged residents, caregivers and women back to work through FWAs?

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment age support
sections.summary: Nearly 88% support a retirement age of 63 and above, and around 80% support a re-employment age of 68 and above, with age discrimination concerns at 63.4%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Nearly 88% support a retirement age of 63 and above, and around 80% support a re-employment age of 68 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The findings also highlighted that concerns relating to negative employer attitudes and age discrimination ranks high at 63.4%.

sections.label: Bringing forward retirement age increase
sections.summary: The current timing of raising the retirement age to 65 may need to be brought forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To facilitate this, we may need to bring forward the current timing of raising the retirement age to 65.

sections.label: Reasonable accommodations and work injury claims
sections.summary: The Tripartite Advisory on Reasonable Accommodations is guidance, not law, and insurers, not MOM, now adjudicate work injury claims.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: As the Tripartite Advisory on Reasonable Accommodations is currently in the form of guidance rather than a legal requirement, it is crucial to monitor its implementation and effectiveness among employers, as well as its impact on individuals with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Additionally, I am curious to know if there are plans to eventually incorporate reasonable accommodations for PwDs into Workplace Fairness Legislation in the future.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Yet, insurers, instead of MOM, are now in charge of adjudicating work injury claims, unlike in the past.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Can the Government release the code of conduct for insurance companies for transparency, including whether there are procedures for workers to hold the insurance companies accountable and the timelines for their claims.

sections.label: Service buyers and freelance safety
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether service buyers and intermediaries should be responsible for the workplace health and safety of freelance or self-employed service providers they engage.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask if the Minister would consider directing service buyers and intermediaries to be responsible for the workplace health and safety of the freelance or self-employed service providers that they engage?

sections.label: Lazada retrenched employees non-compete clause
sections.summary: Retrenched Lazada employees were bound by a 12-month non-compete clause covering many technology, retail and logistics companies beyond key competitors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: A recent example is that of retrenched Lazada employees who were bound by a lengthy 12-month non-compete clause covering an extensive list of technology, retail and logistics companies, which extend far beyond the firm's key competitors, according to a news report.

sections.label: Non-compete clauses and guidelines
sections.summary: Non-compete clauses increasingly appear in mid-level employee contracts, and the Government is developing guidelines on their inclusion in local employment contracts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Perhaps more perniciously, they are now increasingly found even in contracts for mid-level employees, not just top management, where the cost-benefit calculus in permitting such clauses are even more shaky.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: This was amply on display during the recent Lazada trade layoffs, where retrenched workers found themselves bound by a year-long non-compete, adding insult to the injury of losing their job.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The Government, under the tripartite framework, has indicated that it is developing a set of guidelines on the inclusion of non-compete clauses in local employment contracts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: This could be defined by salary of, say, less than $10,000 a month and/or complemented by job scope for all non-C-suite executives.

sections.label: Shopee non-compete clause case
sections.summary: Shopee failed to prevent an employee from joining a rival firm despite non-compete clauses.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Indeed, in a recent case, e-commerce firm Shopee failed to prevent an employee from joining a rival firm despite the presence of non-compete clauses.

sections.label: Raising workmen salary caps
sections.summary: The speaker proposes raising the salary caps of $2,600 and $4,500 in section 35 of the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: First, to raise the salaries caps of workmen and non-workmen prescribed in Part IV of the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I opine that both the salary caps as stipulated in section 35 of $2,600 and $4,500 respectively should be raised.

sections.label: Employer reasons for termination
sections.summary: The speaker proposes requiring employers to give explicit reasons for termination in all employer-initiated cessations of employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: It therefore makes it difficult for employees to bring a case of unfair dismissal against the employer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I propose that employers should be required to give their reasons for termination or discontinuation of employment explicitly in all cases of cessation of employment initiated by the employer.

sections.label: Review of Part IV threshold
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister if there are plans to review the Part IV threshold, last amended in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the Part IV threshold was last amended in 2021, I would like to ask the Minister if there are any plans to review the threshold to reflect current wages and anticipated wage growth.

sections.label: Median monthly bed rentals
sections.summary: Ministry statistics show median monthly rentals for a bed hit $420 at the start of last year, up from $280 four years before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Ministry statistics show that median monthly rentals for a bed hit $420 at the start of last year, up from $280 four years before.

sections.label: Job change before permit expiry
sections.summary: Workers can only obtain a new job without their current employer's consent during the 14- to 21-day window before the work permit expires.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Currently, workers can only obtain a new job without their current employer's consent during the 14- to 21-day window before the work permit expires, meaning the employers who anti-competitively want to prevent other companies from hiring their workers in the future and for a long period to block them from doing so.

sections.label: Dormitory and NSF space standards
sections.summary: Dormitory standards require at least 3.5 square metres per resident, rising 0.1 square metre in six years, while NSFs have at least seven square metres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our current dormitory standards require at least 3.5 square metres per resident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We are asking dormitories to only increase this by 0.1 square metre within the next six years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By contrast, our full-time National Servicemen (NSFs) have at least seven square metres per resident.

sections.label: Workplace fatality rate drop
sections.summary: The annual workplace fatality rate dropped to 0.99 per 100,000 workers in 2023, five years ahead of the WSH 2028 goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I filed numerous Parliamentary Questions (PQs) and raised two Adjournment Motions on the need to keep our workers and workplaces safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I was therefore happy to hear from MOM that the annual workplace fatality rate has dropped to 0.99 per 100,000 workers in 2023, five years ahead of our WSH 2028 goal.

sections.label: Workplace safety demerit point system
sections.summary: In October 2023, the workplace safety demerit point system was extended to the manufacturing sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In October 2023, the workplace safety demerit point system was extended to the manufacturing sector.

sections.label: WIS and PWM income cap
sections.summary: WIS and PWM must go hand in hand to uplift lower-wage workers' wages, and the income qualifying cap rose from $2,500 to $3,000 for those 30 and older.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) and PWM are two important policies that must go hand in hand to uplift the wages of lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: I welcome the raising of the income qualifying cap from $2,500 to $3,000 for those 30 years and older.

sections.label: PWCS ceiling and co-funding rise
sections.summary: Raising the PWCS ceiling from $2,500 to $3,000 and co-funding from 30% to 50% shows commitment to raise lower-wage workers' wages while helping businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: The raising of PWCS ceiling from $2,500 to $3,000 and the raising of the co-funding level for the increase in wages of the lower-wage workers from 30% to 50% shows the Government’s commitment to help increase the wages of the lower-wage workers while helping businesses with this wage cost increase.

sections.label: PWCS ceiling and fund top-up
sections.summary: The planned PWCS wage ceiling increase to $3,000 in 2025, with a $1 billion top-up, underscores commitment to lower-wage workers, giving employers relief and workers stability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the planned increase in the PWCS wage ceiling to $3,000 in 2025, accompanied by a $1 billion top-up to the fund, underscores the Government's commitment to enhancing support for lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This enhancement not only provides financial relief to employers but also empowers workers to pursue higher standards of living and greater financial stability.

sections.label: Resident employment growth sectors
sections.summary: Resident employment grew in sectors with higher productivity or pay, such as financial and professional services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Resident employment grew in sectors with higher productivity or pay, such as financial and professional services.

sections.label: Falling birth rate workforce approach
sections.summary: With the birth rate falling and the workforce set to decline, the sustainable approach is productivity-driven growth, moving local workers up the value chain and taking in complementary foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Our birth rate continues to fall, despite our best efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: If we continue on this trajectory, our workforce will taper off and decline.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The only sustainable approach is to pursue productivity-driven growth and that is enabling our local workers to move up the value chain and taking in foreign workers who can complement our local workers.

sections.label: Overseas Networks Expertise Pass launch
sections.summary: The Overseas Networks and Expertise Pass (ONE Pass) was launched in January 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In January 2023, we launched the Overseas Networks and Expertise Pass (ONE Pass).

sections.label: ONE Pass applications approved
sections.summary: As of 1 January 2024, nearly 4,200 ONE Pass applications have been approved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As of 1 January 2024, we have approved nearly 4,200 ONE Pass applications.

sections.label: EP minimum qualifying salary increase
sections.summary: The EP minimum qualifying salary will rise from $5,000 to $5,600 per month, and in financial services from $5,500 to $6,200 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For EPs, in line with how the benchmarks have moved, we will be increasing the EP minimum qualifying salary from $5,000 to $5,600 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For the financial services sector which has higher wage norms, this will be revised from $5,500 to $6,200 per month.

sections.label: Revised EP salary application dates
sections.summary: The revised EP qualifying salary applies to new EP applications from 1 January 2025 and renewal applications from 1 January 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The revised EP qualifying salary will only apply to new EP applications from 1 January 2025 and to renewal applications from 1 January 2026.

sections.label: EP shortage occupation bonus points
sections.summary: The share of EP holders in shortage occupations rose since COMPASS, with 20% of new EP holders in these occupations using bonus points to pass COMPASS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The proportion of EP holders in shortage occupations has increased since COMPASS was implemented, which shows that the list reflects real shortages in the industry, with 20% of new EP holders in these shortage occupations using the bonus points to pass COMPASS.

sections.label: Work Permit holders surpass 2019
sections.summary: The number of Work Permit holders today has surpassed COVID-19 levels in 2019 by 12.2%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The number of Work Permit holders today has surpassed the COVID-19 levels in 2019 by 12.2%.

sections.label: Marine shipyard DRC and levy changes
sections.summary: The marine shipyard DRC will be reduced from 77.8% to 75% and basic-skilled R2 Marine Shipyard Work Permit holder levy raised from $400 to $500, effective 1 January 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC) for the marine shipyard sector will be gradually reduced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As a first step, the DRC will be reduced from 77.8% to 75%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For basic-skilled R2 Marine Shipyard Work Permit holders, the levy will be increased by $100, from $400 to $500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Changes to the DRC and levies will take effect from 1 January 2026 to give businesses lead time to adjust.

sections.label: Enhanced CCP salary support
sections.summary: CCP salary support caps will rise to $7,500 per month for mature or long-term unemployed workers and $5,000 for other participants, up to $45,000 per worker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To Mr Patrick Tay's suggestion, I am happy to announce that we will be enhancing our CCP to provide greater support to employers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For mature or long-term unemployed workers, the maximum salary support will be raised from $6,000 to $7,500 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For other CCP participants, we will increase the cap from $4,000 to $5,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This means that employers can receive up to $45,000 of salary support for each worker for a six-month conversion programme.

sections.label: CareersFinder first six months usage
sections.summary: In the first six months, more than 15,000 individuals have used CareersFinder.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In the first six months, more than 15,000 individuals have used CareersFinder.

sections.label: Resident employment and unemployment rates
sections.summary: Resident employment expands annually, labour force participation is 68.6%, and in 2023 resident unemployment was 2.7% and long-term unemployment 0.7%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Resident employment is expanded annually, even through the recent pandemic, and our labour force participation remains high at 68.6%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In 2023, the resident unemployment rate was stable and low at 2.7%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The resident long-term unemployment rate also remains low at 0.7%.

sections.label: CPF Full Retirement Sum improvement
sections.summary: The proportion of active CPF members setting aside their Full Retirement Sum at age 55 rose from five in 10 to seven in 10.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Over the last decade, the proportion of active CPF members setting aside their Full Retirement Sum (FRS) at age 55, either fully in cash or a mixture of property and cash, has improved from five in 10, to seven in 10 today.

sections.label: Majulah Package beneficiary numbers
sections.summary: The Majulah Package is now expected to benefit 1.6 million Singaporeans, up from around 1.4 million previously estimated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Majulah Package is now expected to benefit 1.6 million Singaporeans, up from around 1.4 million Singaporeans previously estimated.

sections.label: Closing Special Account principle
sections.summary: The core principle behind closing the SA is to right-site CPF monies so only long-term retirement savings earn the higher long-term interest rate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The core principle behind closing the SA is to "right-site" CPF monies, such that only CPF savings committed for long-term retirement earn the higher long-term interest rate.

sections.label: SA transfer to RA
sections.summary: Only 8,400 high-income members aged 55 and above cannot fully transfer SA savings to their RA, while over 99% can.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Only 8,400 members, who are relatively high-income earners, representing less than 1% of members aged 55 and above, will not be able to fully transfer their SA savings to their RA, as we raise the ERS to four times that of BRS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In other words, more than 99% of CPF members aged 55 and above today will be able to transfer all their SA savings to their RA, to continue earning the higher long-term interest rate and receive higher retirement payouts, should they wish to do so.

sections.label: Raised ERS payouts and liquidity
sections.summary: With the raised ERS, a member turning 55 in 2025 can receive about $3,300 monthly CPF LIFE payouts at 65, up from about $2,500.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: With the raised ERS, a member turning 55 years old in 2025 can receive about $3,300 per month of CPF LIFE payouts at age 65, if he chooses to top up to the raised ERS, up from about $2,500 today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We recognise that close to 720,000 members with withdrawable SA balances, with a median balance of about $2,000, may experience some loss in liquidity.

sections.label: Earn and Save Bonus
sections.summary: The Earn and Save Bonus is up to $1,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: First, the Earn and Save Bonus of up to $1,000 per year.

sections.label: Retirement and MediSave bonuses
sections.summary: A one-time Retirement Savings Bonus of up to $1,500 and a one-time MediSave Bonus of up to $1,500 are provided for those with lower CPF retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Second, a one-time Retirement Savings Bonus of up to $1,500 for those with lower CPF retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Third, a one-time MediSave Bonus of up to $1,500.

sections.label: Enhanced Matched Retirement Savings Scheme
sections.summary: An additional $260 million will be spent, raising 2025 spending to around $860 million, and the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme's annual matching cap will rise from $600 to $2,000 and extend to those older than 70.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will spend an additional $260 million, spending a total of around $860 million in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will enhance the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) by increasing the annual matching cap from $600 to $2,000 per year and extending the scheme to those who are older than 70 years old.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This will double the number of eligible Singaporeans to about 800,000 per year.

sections.label: CPF Investment Scheme
sections.summary: CPF members willing to take on more investment risk for potentially higher returns can participate in the CPF Investment Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: CPF members who have the appetite to take on more investment risk for potentially higher returns can participate in the CPF Investment Scheme.

sections.label: CPF interest rates versus market
sections.summary: Over two decades of low interest rates, CPF paid 2.5% interest plus extra interest, with the annual OA rate averaging 1.7 percentage points above 12-month fixed deposit rates from 1999 to 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Over the past two decades of low-interest rate environment, we have paid 2.5% interest, as well as extra interest, while the market was paying well below that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: On average, the annual OA interest rate was 1.7 percentage points higher than the 12-month fixed deposit rates, from 1999 to 2021.

sections.label: HPS applications not approved
sections.summary: In the last three years, about 1.2% of HPS applications were not approved due to serious pre-existing medical conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In the last three years, about 1.2% of HPS applications were not approved due to serious pre-existing medical conditions.

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: In 2026, the retirement age will increase from 63 to 64 and the re-employment age from 68 to 69.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In 2026, the retirement age will be increased from 63 to 64, while the re-employment age will be increased from 68 to 69.

sections.label: New OMIP for overseas roles
sections.summary: The Government will launch a new OMIP to support currently employed people taking on overseas roles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If you are currently employed, the Government will launch a new OMIP to support you in taking on overseas roles and expanding your horizons.

sections.label: Support for lower-wage and older workers
sections.summary: PWM, higher LQS, enhanced WIS and the $8.2 billion Majulah Package with three components will support lower-wage and older workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For lower-wage workers, the PWM can provide you with better income security and career progression.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This year, we will raise the LQS and enhance WIS to provide additional support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If you are currently over 50 years old, we will provide greater support through the Majulah Package.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This $8.2 billion package consists of the following three components: First, if you continue working and earn a monthly salary of $6,000 or less, you will receive an Earn and Save Bonus of up to $1,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Second, Singaporeans who have not yet attained the Basic Retirement Sum in their CPF accounts can receive a one-time Retirement Savings Bonus of up to $1,500.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Third, all Singaporeans above 50 years old this year can receive a one-time MediSave Bonus of up to $1,500 to help you with medical and insurance expenses.

sections.label: MOM speech on lower-wage workers
sections.summary: The speaker will elaborate on the tripartite approach to uplifting lower-wage workers, HR capabilities and WSH progress.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, earlier, the Minister for Manpower outlined how MOM will strengthen efforts to uplift our lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In my speech, I will elaborate on the positive impact of our tripartite approach to uplifting lower-wage workers and how we will build on our efforts; secondly, how we have strengthened our HR capabilities; and third, our progress in improving WSH.

sections.label: Real income growth of lower-wage workers
sections.summary: Real incomes of lower-wage workers at the 20th percentile rose cumulatively 30% from 2013 to 2023, faster than the median worker's 22%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Real incomes of lower-wage workers at the 20th percentile have risen cumulatively by 30% from 2013 to 2023, faster than the median worker at 22%.

sections.label: PWM coverage of lower-wage workers
sections.summary: More than 155,000 lower-wage workers across nine sectors and occupations are covered by the PWM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Today, more than 155,000 lower-wage workers across nine sectors and occupations are covered by the PWM.

sections.label: Raising LQS thresholds
sections.summary: The LQS threshold will be raised from $1,400 to $1,600 for full-time and from $9 to $10.50 per hour for part-time local employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As announced by the Deputy Prime Minister at Budget, the LQS threshold will be raised from $1,400 to $1,600 for full-time local employees to better support our lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We will also raise the LQS threshold for part-time local employees, from $9 per hour to $10.50 per hour.

sections.label: Higher qualifying income cap
sections.summary: From 2025, the qualifying monthly income cap for WIS and WSS rises from $2,500 to $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: From 2025, we will raise the qualifying monthly income cap further, from $2,500 to $3,000, for both WIS and WSS.

sections.label: PWCS disbursed for 2022 wage increases
sections.summary: For 2022 wage increases, about $1 billion of PWCS was disbursed, co-funding increases for over 345,000 employees by over 70,000 employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For wage increases given in 2022, the Government disbursed about $1 billion of PWCS to employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: This co-funded the wage increases given to more than 345,000 employees by over 70,000 employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The median monthly wage increase supported by PWCS was about $300.

sections.label: Enhanced co-funding and wage ceiling
sections.summary: The Government will co-fund up to 50% of 2024 wage increases for eligible lower-wage workers and raise the 2025 and 2026 wage ceiling to $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With this year’s enhancement, the Government will co-fund up to 50% of wage increases given by employers to eligible lower-wage workers in 2024, up from the original 30%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Second, we will raise the wage ceiling in 2025 and 2026 to $3,000, up from $2,500 per month.

sections.label: Workplace fatal injury rate 2023
sections.summary: In 2023, the workplace fatal injury rate fell to 0.99 per 100,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In 2023, our workplace fatal injury rate fell to 0.99 per 100,000 workers.

sections.label: Lower-wage worker real income growth
sections.summary: Real incomes of lower-wage workers rose cumulatively by 30% from 2013 to 2023, faster than the median worker's 22%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Real incomes of lower-wage workers have risen cumulatively by 30% from 2013 to 2023, faster than the median worker at 22%.

sections.label: PWM coverage today
sections.summary: Today, 155,000 lower-wage workers across nine sectors and occupations are covered by a PWM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Today, 155,000 lower-wage workers across nine sectors and occupations are covered by a PWM.

sections.label: LQS threshold increase
sections.summary: The LQS threshold rises to $1,600 for full-time and $10.50 per hour for part-time local employees from 1 July 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: First, we will raise the LQS threshold from $1,400 to $1,600 for full-time local employees from 1 July 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We will also raise the LQS threshold for part-time local employees, from $9 per hour to $10.50 per hour.

sections.label: Majulah Package for seniors
sections.summary: The Government will introduce the Majulah Package to support young seniors and Pioneer and Merdeka generation seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To boost the retirement adequacy of our seniors, the Government will introduce the Majulah Package to provide more support for our "young seniors", as well as seniors in the Pioneer and Merdeka generations.

sections.label: Senior workers' CPF contribution rates
sections.summary: The planned increase in senior workers' CPF contribution rates will continue so they can accumulate more in their CPF accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: First, to allow senior workers to accumulate more in their CPF accounts, we will continue with the planned increase in senior workers' CPF contribution rates.

sections.label: Scheme benefits and matching grants
sections.summary: About 172,000 Singaporeans benefited in the first three years, with matching grants of about $200 million provided thus far.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In the first three years, about 172,000 Singaporeans have benefited from the scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Government has provided matching grants of about $200 million thus far.

sections.label: Maximum matching grant quantum
sections.summary: The maximum matching grant quantum will be increased from $600 to $2,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Second, Mr Desmond Choo would be glad to hear that the maximum matching grant quantum will be increased from $600 to $2,000 per year.

sections.label: MRSS enhancement from 2025
sections.summary: From 2025 the MRSS annual matching limit for eligible elderly Singaporeans' Retirement Accounts rises to $2,000, with a $20,000 lifetime limit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Government will enhance the MRSS starting from 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The annual matching limit for eligible elderly Singaporeans' Retirement Accounts will be raised to $2,000, with a lifetime limit of $20,000.

sections.label: Elderly cash top-up savings
sections.summary: Eligible elderly Singaporeans receiving $2,000 annually in cash top-up will gain about $48,000 in retirement savings over 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: If eligible elderly Singaporeans receive $2,000 in cash top-up annually, their retirement savings will increase by about $48,000 over 10 years.

sections.label: SSS payment increase 2025
sections.summary: From 2025 the SSS quarterly payment rises 20% for inflation, with an extra $260 million in 2025 and total annual expenditure of $860 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Starting from 2025, the SSS quarterly payment will increase by 20% to help cope with inflation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To achieve this, the Government will allocate an additional $260 million in 2025 with total annual expenditure reaching $860 million.

sections.label: Employment Act regular review
sections.summary: The Government regularly reviews the Employment Act with tripartite partners, considering changes in work nature, workplace arrangements and workforce profiles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Government reviews the Employment Act regularly together with our tripartite partners, taking into account changes in the nature of work, workplace arrangements and workforce profiles.

sections.label: Guidelines on clause use
sections.summary: Tripartite partners are releasing guidelines on the use of such clauses in the second half of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Members would be aware that tripartite partners are releasing guidelines on the use of such clauses in the second half of this year.

sections.label: Migrant worker housing moves
sections.summary: MOM expanded the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act to cover dormitories housing more than six workers and announced the Dormitory Transition Scheme for almost 1,000 dormitories by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: MOM has made significant moves in migrant worker housing in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We expanded the scope of the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act to cover all dormitories housing more than six workers to ensure dormitories are well-managed with good health and safety standards in place.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We also announced the Dormitory Transition Scheme to transition almost 1,000 existing dormitories to improve standards by the year 2030.

sections.label: More purpose-built dormitory places
sections.summary: About 47,000 more places will be available over the next few years as seven more purpose-built dormitories come into operation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: About 47,000 more will be available over the next few years, as seven more purpose-built dormitories come into operation.

sections.label: Dormitory minimum living space standards
sections.summary: Setting minimum living space per dormitory resident balances liveability against costs and land-take, and the new standards align with International Labour Organization workers' housing standards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In setting the minimum living space per resident for dormitories, we have to balance liveability against costs and land-take considerations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The new dormitory standards are in line with the standards set by the International Labour Organization for workers' housing.

sections.label: Penalties for affected workers
sections.summary: Offenders may be sentenced to up to two years' imprisonment, fines up to $30,000, or both per worker affected, though courts have not imposed maximum penalties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Currently, offenders may be sentenced to imprisonment of up to two years, fines of up to $30,000, or both, for each worker affected.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Thus far, the penalties imposed by the Courts have not reached the maximum fine or the imprisonment term.

sections.label: Migrant worker healthcare and outreach
sections.summary: Since 2022 the Primary Care Plan was implemented to improve migrant workers' healthcare access and the Friends of ACE network was established to expand outreach.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Since 2022, we have implemented the Primary Care Plan to improve access to healthcare for migrant workers and established the Friends of ACE network to expand our outreach efforts.

sections.label: Raising retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: Retirement and re-employment ages were raised to 63 and 68 in 2022, and tripartite partners agreed to raise them to 64 and 69 in 2026, toward 65 and 70 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2022, we raised the retirement and re-employment ages to 63 and 68 respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: As announced by Minister Tan See Leng, the tripartite partners have agreed to raise the retirement and re-employment ages further to 64 and 69, respectively, in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: This will bring us another step closer to our eventual goal of setting retirement and re-employment ages at 65 and 70, respectively, by 2030.

sections.label: Employer grant support amount
sections.summary: Employers can enjoy up to $125,000 in grant support under the scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Employers can enjoy up to $125,000 in grant support under the scheme.

sections.label: Disbursements to senior-hiring employers
sections.summary: In 2023, $315 million was disbursed, benefiting about 90,000 employers that hire more than 400,000 senior workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: In 2023, we disbursed $315 million, benefiting about 90,000 employers that hire more than 400,000 senior workers.

sections.label: CPF matching grant enhancements
sections.summary: Enhanced matching grants of $2,000 yearly and $20,000 lifetime cap can raise eligible seniors' CPF savings by about $48,000 over 10 years, giving about $260 extra monthly payout.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The enhancements to provide the $2,000 per year matching grant annually and $20,000 matching grant over a lifetime as a cap are, in fact, a significant increase from the current scheme and can help to increase eligible seniors' CPF savings, as I had explained in my main speech, by about $48,000 over 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This is already going to give them about $260 of extra payout per month.

sections.label: Family top-ups for ineligible seniors
sections.summary: Family members can top up a senior's CPF account and enjoy tax benefits of up to $16,000 a year for top-ups that do not attract MRSS matching grants.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For those who may already have a certain quantum in their CPF and they are not eligible, for example, for the MRSS, what certain family members can do is to continue to top up the senior's account and enjoy tax benefits of up to $16,000 a year for those kind of top-ups that do not attract any matching grants from the MRSS.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits survey findings
sections.summary: From the survey, nine in 10, or 90%, pay retrenchment benefits, typically ranging from about two weeks to a month per year of service.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: From the survey, nine in 10, or 90%, of them pay the retrenchment benefits, typically ranging from about two weeks to a month per year of service.

sections.label: Update on MAST safe measures
sections.summary: MOM is asked to provide an update on the MAST safe measures implemented and their effectiveness since implementation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: One, can MOM provide an update on the MAST safe measures that were implemented and what is their effectiveness since implementation?

sections.label: Workplace fatality injury rate
sections.summary: The workplace fatality injury rate fell to 0.99 per 100,000, placing Singapore among the top four around the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Our workplace fatality injury rate fell to 0.99 per 100,000, which puts us among the top four around the world.

sections.label: Mandatory leadership training for leaders
sections.summary: For many leaders, especially in critical, high-risk industries, all leaders and CEOs must undergo the top leaders' leadership training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: What is more important is that we have to engage all stakeholders to press on with the efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Therefore, for many of our leaders, especially in critical, high-risk industries, we have already made it mandatory for all leaders and CEOs to be put through the top leaders' leadership training.

sections.label: Leader accountability in construction
sections.summary: Following HSP, accountability was raised at leader level and extended down to all subcontracting levels in construction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Because leaders decide on the resources, leaders invest in the kind of equipment, processes, how the workers work and what kind of construction methods you use, for example, are all determined at the top.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Therefore, among the things that we have done, following HSP, was to up the accountability, not just at the worker level, but also at the leader level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If you look at construction, for example, we made it so that there is accountability down to all the subcontracting levels, and not just at the first- or second-layer subcontractors.

sections.label: Mandatory video surveillance in construction
sections.summary: For sectors such as construction, mandatory video surveillance has been put in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For sectors, such as construction, for example, we have put in place video surveillance, which is mandatory now.

sections.label: Caregiving leave and flexible work support
sections.summary: In 2022, 59% of employers voluntarily gave extra paid caregiving leave, over 4,000 adopted a Tripartite Standard, and 85% of caregivers preferred FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In 2022, about 59% of employers voluntarily provided additional paid caregiving leave, such as family care leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: More than 4,000 employers have also adopted the Tripartite Standard on Unpaid Leave for Unexpected Care Needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We know that in a survey, a recent one by NTUC, 85% of working caregivers indicated that FWAs were their most preferred mode of support compared to paid caregiving leave, which was favoured by 64% of caregivers.

sections.label: CPFIS SA investments at retirement
sections.summary: Members may hold existing CPFIS SA investments until sale or maturity, when proceeds go to the RA up to the Full Retirement Sum, with the balance to the OA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Members can continue to hold their existing CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) SA investments until they decide to sell or when the investment matures, upon which the proceeds will then be paid to the member's RA, up to the Full Retirement Sum.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Any remaining balance will be paid to the OA.

sections.label: Tripartite Guidelines on FWA requests
sections.summary: The Tripartite Guidelines will require proper consideration of FWA requests and not mandate employers to provide FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The Tripartite Guidelines will focus on requiring proper consideration of FWA requests and not mandating the employers to provide FWAs.

sections.label: Handling non-compliant employers
sections.summary: A calibrated and enabling approach will be applied initially, with templates, guides and training, and TAFEP will guide breaching employers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling also asked about employers that do not comply with the Tripartite Guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We will apply a calibrated and enabling approach, at least, in the initial implementation of the Tripartite Guidelines, which will include providing employers with templates, guides and training to equip them to comply with the Guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In the event of breaches, employees may seek help from TAFEP, and TAFEP will then reach out and guide these employers to put in place proper processes as well as to reassess the requests for flexible work arrangements by their employees.

sections.label: CPF interest rates and GIC returns
sections.summary: Government uses its buffer of net assets to give CPF members fair and stable interest rates, since GIC returns fluctuate yearly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For the 20 years of historical returns, even though GIC has exceeded CPF interest rates, there is no guarantee that GIC's future returns will always exceed CPF interest rates in every year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, if we pass some of these returns directly to members, there will be significant year-to-year fluctuations in the interest rate that members receive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, what the Government has done is that it has used our buffer of net assets to ensure that CPF members receive fair and stable interest rates to grow CPF balances for retirement adequacy.

sections.label: Citizens' Panel career proposals
sections.summary: The Citizens' Panel proposed a career gym and a skills passport, which were taken on board to design career health and CareersFinder.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: One, the Citizens' Panel proposed a career gym where our local citizens can go on to first understand what their career prospects are, given their qualifications and how they can continue to work at it to improve their career prospects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Second, a skills passport, both of which, in terms of the suggestions that the Citizens' Panel raised, we have taken on board to design career health and also the CareersFinder.

sections.label: Choosing electricians for scoping
sections.summary: Electricians were chosen because what is required has been scoped out with the different agencies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I will keep the first one very short because I want to dedicate more time to the second one.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We chose electricians because it is one where we have scoped out what is required with the different agencies.

sections.label: Worker support and retirement age
sections.summary: WSG services, CareersFinder, Career Health and CCPs help workers, and a jobseeker support scheme and higher retirement age are coming.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: You have the WSG Career Matching Services, the CareersFinder, Career Health and there is a whole slew of CCPs to help our workers, where we subsidise up to 90% of salary and course fee support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are going to be introducing a jobseeker support scheme to empower those that are involuntarily unemployed to bounce back into employment, which the Deputy Prime Minister will announce later this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If you are a senior at the end of your work-life cycle, if you want to continue to work, we are raising the retirement age.
